delay.title: TV delay
delay.help: Hold the page, the team radio and your automations back to match your TV or stream. Everyone in the house shares this setting.

spoiler.standingsCap: No-spoiler mode: the standings before this weekend.

settings.title: Settings
settings.running: Connected to F1's live timing for the session under way.
settings.waiting: Ready: it connects by itself when a session starts.
settings.pausedHelp: Paused: nothing connects to F1 and nothing live is written to disk.
settings.autoStartHelp: Live timing turns itself on when a session is about to start. Pausing it during a session holds until the next one.
settings.f1tvHelp: Only the live track map needs F1TV; everything else works without an account.
settings.tokenReplace: Paste a new token to replace the current one
settings.tokenSteps: Sign in at f1tv.formula1.com, open the browser's developer tools → Application (Storage in Firefox) → Cookies, and copy the value of loginSession. It is renewed automatically; it is never shown again after saving.
settings.removeConfirm: Remove the F1TV token? The live map stops until a new one is added.
settings.entitiesHelp: Use them in automations and dashboards: flags, safety car, penalties and the stewards' decisions have their own entities. They follow the TV delay and no-spoiler mode.

errors.token_invalid: That does not look like an F1TV token. Paste the whole value of the loginSession cookie.
errors.token_expired: This token has expired or expires within minutes. Sign in to F1TV again and copy a fresh one.
errors.token_no_subscription: This F1TV account has no active subscription.
errors.remove_failed: The token could not be removed. Try again in a moment.

settings.sidebar: Show Live Board in the sidebar
settings.sidebarHelp: Off: the panel still opens from the integration's device page, and the cards keep working on dashboards.
settings.adminPanel: Only administrators can open the panel
settings.adminPanelHelp: Off (the default): every user of the house sees Live Board. On: only administrators do. The cards follow the visibility of the dashboard they are on.

cards.mapAfter: The map is live only: it comes back at the next session.
cards.mapNeedsF1tv: The live map needs F1TV: an administrator can add a token in the panel's Settings.

time.title: Times
time.home: As in my Home Assistant profile ({zone})
time.bothHelp: Next to each time, in small, the other one: the track's local time, or yours when you chose the track's.

drivers.title: My drivers
drivers.help: Follow up to five drivers: each gets a sensor with position, gap, tyre and pits, and the “My drivers” event fires when they gain or lose a place, take the lead, pit, set the fastest lap, retire or get a penalty. Their rows have a ★ in the timing tower.
drivers.lossCircuit: Estimate: a stop costs about {loss} s at this circuit.
drivers.lossGeneric: Estimate: a stop costs about {loss} s (a generic figure).
drivers.pitting: {n} cars in the pits: less certain.

summary.title: Summary at the end of a session
summary.help: When a session ends: podium, fastest lap, retirements, penalties and your drivers, sent to the notify services you choose. It is also the “Session summary” event, for your own automations.
summary.noServices: No notify service in this Home Assistant (the mobile app adds one per phone).
summary.testSent: Sent: the summary of what the Live page shows.
summary.testNothing: Nothing to summarise yet: it needs a session on the Live page.
summary.spoiler: With no-spoiler mode on, the summary waits until you reveal the session or turn the mode off.
summary.testHidden: Not sent: no-spoiler mode hides the Live page.
summary.compactHelp: Podium, fastest lap, retirements, penalties and your drivers.
summary.fullHelp: The same, then the whole classification with every driver's time: gap and best lap in a race, best lap and gap in qualifying and practice.

kiosk.title: Dedicated screen
kiosk.help: For a TV, a monitor with a Raspberry Pi or a wall tablet: this address opens the panel on the whole screen, over Home Assistant's sidebar, with the pointer hidden when it rests. On a Raspberry Pi: chromium --kiosk followed by the address. The ⛶ button in the header does the same for a moment.
kiosk.options: Add &page=calendar to open another page, &scale=1.3 to make everything bigger on a TV.
kiosk.small: For a small screen (an ESP32 with ESPHome, e-paper): enable the “Small screen” sensor. It carries the state of the Live page and short fields ready to print: lap, track status and its colour, the top ten as rows, your drivers, the next session. The guide has an ESPHome example.

circuit.title: Circuit history
circuit.explain: Affinity index: 50 = as the car that year; higher = the circuit suits the driver, lower = it does not.
circuit.howText: For every year a driver raced here, the car's level is the team's place in that season's constructors' championship, two cars per team: first place expects P1.5, fifth P9.5. The race counts for 60% and qualifying for 40%: places gained or lost on that level. A retirement counts only when it is the driver's doing (an accident, a collision, a spin, a disqualification); mechanical failures are left out. Recent years weigh more: each year back counts 15% less. The index is 50 plus 5 points for every place better than the car, from 0 to 100; with few races it is pulled towards 50 (one race keeps a third of the distance, eight keep 80%), so one good afternoon does not top the list. Years with no constructors' championship (before 1958) do not count.
circuit.racesHelp: Races counted in the index / races here
circuit.gridPenalty: Grid worse than qualifying: a penalty or a pit-lane start
circuit.penaltiesUnknown: Not available: before 2018, or no detail in F1's archive
circuit.expectedHelp: The car's level that year and the places gained (▲) or lost (▼) on it in the race; Q is qualifying.
circuit.legend: ▼ next to the grid: worse than qualifying (a penalty or a pit-lane start). vs car: the car's expected place and the places gained (▲) or lost (▼) on it; Q is qualifying. Penalties from 2018; — when F1's archive has no detail.
